approval_required_for: Any DUT RTL change to block_input lifecycle/start sequencing, connected-kernel scheduler, mlp_down valid/ready, residual/output logic, or AXI/DDR integration before the exact replay proves causal ownership.
Any semantic change to the kernel_start_precedes_stage0_input contract rather than a schema correction that aligns it with the authoritative accepted-input-before-start invariant.

Any architecture, pipeline schedule, memory layout, numeric policy, tolerance, checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, golden output, testbench contract, or exact board-wrapper/source-hash change.
Any promotion or execution of dependent higher gates before current functional_sim and current CCTG boundary closure pass.

observations: The exact user-supplied sample wrapper identity passed, with complete source and simulation-closure hashes. It must remain unchanged; no simplified AXI/DDR wrapper is permitted.

The current exact-board VCS run compiled successfully but failed functional_sim with a proven intra-layer pipeline violation: 16 of 16 tokens and 1792 of 1792 core ingress beats completed by cycle 20805737, while output_ready was 1 and output accepted zero beats. This is a current board-layer liveness failure, not a timeout-only classification.

The current direct trace shows kernel start accepted, core ingress accepted 1792 beats, and core egress ready, but no core egress valid or accepted beat. The inner-cone observation reports mlp_down_input_accepted_count=607, mlp_down_input_terminal_fire_count=0, and mlp_down_output_accepted_count=0; this localizes the next observation scope but does not prove an RTL owner.

The first CCTG failure is kernel_start_precedes_stage0_input at transaction 0 and cycle 20572946, with stage0 input and core ingress firing while kernel_start_to_core was 0. However, hierarchical learning context requires an accepted input handshake before lifecycle start, and the same trace has first_start_cycle=20572948 after first input/core ingress at 20572946. The recorded expectation is therefore inconsistent with the authoritative lifecycle invariant and cannot justify a block_input patch.

The exact-sample testbench contract and dynamic evidence checks failed because observability schema and current-DAG boundary declarations are incomplete or invalid. This is a verification-capability repair issue until a corrected, simulation-only trace proves a DUT-side violation.

Operator-leaf and connected single-layer certificates remain reusable. The completed lower-layer recheck passed 1792 ingress and 1792 egress beats with pipeline overlap, and no current hash-bound trace validly contradicts a named lower-layer invariant after accounting for the disputed lifecycle contract.

Runtime load and independent AXI/prefetch progress do not establish output-frontier progress or a hardware pass. The loaded-word evidence must remain bound to the existing loader manifest; no weight, input, expected output, or numeric policy artifact may be regenerated.

The authoritative SACG memory contains eight open same-scope retry requests and 24 active contamination barriers. Rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts are diagnostic evidence only and cannot be consumed as validated design inputs; refined current-stage artifacts may supersede them only after current checks pass.
proposed_actions: Repair the simulation-only debug observability contract so lifecycle ordering, direct core ingress/egress, the 13 planned dataflow boundaries, token order, and the named mlp_down tail are schema-valid and bound to the current exact source closure.

Run one bounded exact-wrapper causal replay using the immutable checkpoint, stimulus fingerprint, target-model reference, numeric policy, semantic testbench, loader manifest, and exact board wrapper hashes. Reconcile whether the valid earliest frontier is lifecycle ordering or post-ingress connected-kernel liveness.

Only after replay reconciliation passes, rerun the current exact-board functional_sim and evidence analyzer. Keep case_multilayer_functional, pipeline_deadlock, AXI protocol, DDR roundtrip, and board semantic aggregation blocked until functional_sim and the current boundary contract close.

If and only if corrected replay proves a DUT-side lifecycle or pipeline contract violation, create a separate approval-gated causal RTL repair for the named owner and rerun the same current board layer. Do not infer or apply that repair now.
risks: Patching block_input based on kernel_start_precedes_stage0_input could reverse the accepted-input-before-start lifecycle invariant and damage a certified integration contract.

Patching mlp_down or any output module from the downstream zero-output symptom would violate causal ownership rules because the current trace lacks a complete valid boundary contract and direct causal proof.

The exact-board run has no functional, numeric, output-count, AXI-order, DDR-roundtrip, or complete-scope board weight-consumption pass. No promotion to synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime ABI, or board runtime is allowed.
The current debug observability contract is not simulation/testbench-only and lacks a valid current-DAG declaration; repairing this capability must not alter DUT semantics or acceptance tolerance.

A checker or golden-reference capability gap must not be misclassified as hardware correctness. Target-model inference, checkpoint, deterministic stimulus, numeric comparison policy, and expected outputs remain immutable.

The accelerator scope remains Transformer blocks only. Do not add embedding, tokenization, final norm, LM head, logits, sampling, or other model-tail work to the DUT or its weight/golden requirements.

constraints: exact user-supplied sample wrapper and selected simulation source closure remain hash-bound
checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, golden, and testbench contract remain immutable
